body: I think the attached PR addresses all your issues. Would you mind trying it out to see?

@xaviershay 
Re example: its a complex setup and hard to recreate outside of Logstash. However, this [line in our test.rake](https://github.com/elastic/logstash/blob/master/rakelib/test.rake#L63) is the starting point.
This is my modified version that loops on `Runner.run`
```rake
  desc "run all installed plugins specs in a separate rspec run, args:['format']"
  task "plugins-separate", [:format] => ["setup"] do  |t, args|
    format = args.format || "documentation"
    # additionally we could have an output file path as an arg
    exit_code = 0

    plugins_to_exclude = ENV.fetch("EXCLUDE_PLUGIN", "").split(",")
    # grab all spec files using the live plugins gem specs. this allows correclty also running the specs
    # of a local plugin dir added using the Gemfile :path option. before this, any local plugin spec would
    # not be run because they were not under the vendor/bundle/jruby/2.0/gems path

    STDERR.puts "starting..."
    i = 1
    test_files = LogStash::PluginManager.find_plugins_gem_specs.shuffle.each do |spec|

      if plugins_to_exclude.size > 0 && plugins_to_exclude.include?(Pathname.new(spec.gem_dir).basename.to_s)
        next
      end

      test_files = Rake::FileList[File.join(spec.gem_dir, "spec/{input,filter,codec,output}s/*_spec.rb")]

      rspec_args = ["--color", "--order", "rand", "--deprecation-out", "data/deprecations-out.txt", "--format", format, test_files]

      STDERR.puts "----------------- #{i} Running #{spec.gem_dir}"

      begin
        exit_code += RSpec::Core::Runner.run(rspec_args)
      rescue => e
        STDERR.puts e.message
        STDERR.puts e.backtrace.take(8)
        STDERR.puts "----------------- #{i}"
      end

      RSpec.clear_examples
      i = i.succ
    end

    STDERR.puts "done..."
    exit(exit_code == 0 ? 0 : 1)
  end
```
Re `RSpec.reset`, tried it but as you suspect configuration that is modified with `require "logstash/devutils/rspec/spec_helper"` is lost.
It would be cool to be able to have a callable be registered with the configuration (once in a require) and this callable is called for each run. We would be less at the mercy of require vs load.
I will attempt to try the PR.

@xaviershay 
I tried your PR.

1) Deprecation accumulation: fixed.
2) RSpec configuration issues: fixed IMO.
3) `--out` IO early close: fixed.

However, because the [file is opened with "w"](https://github.com/rspec/rspec-core/blob/master/lib/rspec/core/formatters.rb#L252) each run overwrites the previous one.
Changing "w" to "a" worked for me but I am not sure how this affects other use cases.

Further observations, when doing multiple runs like this, especially with the progress format, its not easy to correlate loop info (`spec.gem_dir` from above example) with the text in the `--out` file.
In the loop I tried to write  `"----------------- #{i} Running #{spec.gem_dir}"` to the `--out` file using:
`RSpec.configuration.output_stream` but this was set to $stdout;
`RSpec.configuration.formatters.first.output`, this works but incurs the cost of [formatters.dup](https://github.com/rspec/rspec-core/blob/master/lib/rspec/core/configuration.rb#L896) for each call.

I considered suggesting adding a preamble command line arg that would be output with the run options prelude but I think that would get messy.

I am not sure you should change this because now that the IO is not closed The RSpec team advice should probably be to create, use and inject ones own IO instance to the run method for these complex cases, e.g. `RSpec::Core::Runner.run(rspec_args, $stderr, io)`. I tested this with File.new and `"a"` everything works as desired.

Thank you!

> Changing "w" to "a" worked for me but I am not sure how this affects other use cases.

In regular usage (running the same suite multiple times), I'd expect the file to be overwritten as it is now.

> The RSpec team advice should probably be to create, use and inject ones own IO instance to the run method for these complex cases, e.g. RSpec::Core::Runner.run(rspec_args, $stderr, io).

Yup :) Out of curiosity, how were you configuring it before? With a command line option?

@xaviershay 

You're welcome.

Ignore the "a" - I think the advice should be "create and inject your own IO instead of using --out"

and yes, before using my own IO instance I used the --out in the rspec_args array.

In terms of advice I mean in the relishapp doc page [running-specs-multiple-times-with-different-runner-options-in-the-same-process](https://www.relishapp.com/rspec/rspec-core/v/3-5/docs/running-specs-multiple-times-with-different-runner-options-in-the-same-process)
I'm going to mark this as closed in preference for #2368
